metaTitle: Fussikur: The Bowiri Migration Festival in the Oti Region
metaDescription: Fussikur is the week-long festival of the Bowiri people of the Oti Region, remembering their migration from Moree. Held between February and March.
subtitle: Bowiri remembers its journey
answer: Fussikur is the festival of the Bowiri people of the Biakoye District in the Oti Region. It remembers their migration from their ancestral home at Moree, in today’s Central Region, to Bowiri Amanforo. It runs for a week between February and March, and ends with a grand durbar of chiefs and people.
facts: Between February and March; lasts a week

schema.description: Week-long festival of the Bowiri people remembering their migration from Moree.

days.label: First Friday
days.title: Confinement
days.html: Chiefs, queen mothers and priests go into confinement.[[1]]

days.label: Tuesday
days.title: Wailing
days.html: A day of wailing for the dead.[[1]]

days.label: Thursday
days.title: The old settlement
days.html: A trip to the old settlement and the shrines on Mount Fortorkpa.[[1]]

days.label: Second Friday
days.title: The stools
days.html: The black stools are cleansed and purified.[[1]]

days.label: Saturday
days.title: Grand durbar
days.html: Each town and clan carries its divisional chief through the main streets in a palanquin, led by Asafo companies with drums, songs, dancing and musketry; the Omanhene’s palanquin comes last. The senior priest pours libation and opens the durbar, the chiefs and queen mothers pay homage to the Omanhene, and he gives his address to the state. Asafo companies dance to show the bravery of the Bowiri.[[1]]

sections.title: Good to know if you go
tips: Where: Bowiri is in the Biakoye District. See the Oti page for places nearby.
Also in Bowiri: Hyirebo, the festival of peace, in April.
Check the dates: the traditional council sets them each year. Local radio and the national press carry the announcement.
Respect the rites: some rituals are sacred and not for cameras. Ask before photographing chiefs, priests or anyone taking part, and follow what the ushers ask.
